text:
opsbot: :rotating_light: automated alert — runtime-prod scheduler P50 spike detected (baseline ~45ms -> 320ms) at 1762103400, p95/p99 also elevated
eli: ugh, I see a lot of microbatch queues backing up on gpu-pool-3
mira: noticed increase in admission_rejects around the same time — any recent rollout?
raj: pushed admission-control tweak earlier this morning (commit a1b2c3) to reduce bursts, suspected fairness fix
hao: linking profiler snapshot: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1762103456/ -- grabbing flamegraphs now
sylvia: quick perf dump:
```
# top hotspots (avg)
scheduler.cpp:select_kernel 45.7%
batcher.cpp:attempt_merge 22.3%
kv_cache.cpp:lookup 12.1%
executor.cpp:enqueue 8.6%
```
eli: select_kernel up that high is surprising — should be <10% normally
mira: batcher.attempt_merge increase might indicate microbatch sizing oscillation, causing more kernel selection work
raj: admission-control change lowered max_inflight per worker from 64 -> 32, might be causing more microbatches and extra kernel switches
hao: I also see kv_cache.hits drop from 98% -> 75% at the same window — possible invalidation storm?
sylvia: could be noisy neighbor evicting KV shards on the same node, causing cache thrash
eli: can we reproduce on canary? I’ll toggle the commit flag to revert admission-control on canary pool now
mira: logs from canary after revert: p50 back to 48ms within 3m :thumbsup:
raj: rollback scheduled to prod via /deploybot rollback a1b2c3 — doing staged rollback to gpu-pool-3 first
opsbot: deploybot: rollback started for runtime-prod@gpu-pool-3 by @raj
hao: while we wait, run small A/B test: run synthetic load with varied microbatch targets (8/16/32) and capture kernel-selection counts
sylvia: capturing KV cache eviction metrics during A/B: `redis:evicts`, `kv_cache.eviction_rate` in grafana panel "runtime/cache"
eli: experiment results: microbatch=8 => kernel switches per second +120%, p50 280ms; microbatch=32 => kernel switches -30%, p50 46ms
mira: that aligns: smaller microbatches increase scheduling churn and kernel selection overhead; admission cap 32 forces those small microbatches during bursty tails
raj: prod rollback to a1b2c3 reverted successfully on gpu-pool-3 — opsbot shows metrics normalizing
opsbot: :white_check_mark: rollback complete; runtime-prod p50 back to 50ms (within 8 minutes)
hao: root-cause hypothesis: admission-control change inadvertently increased microbatch fragmentation under bursty arrival patterns, increasing kernel selection overhead + KV cache churn (noisy neighbor amplified cache misses)
sylvia: mitigation: revert commit (done), add adaptive admission which considers recent microbatch merge rate and kv_cache.hit_ratio before reducing inflight cap
eli: action items:
- raj: open PR for adaptive admission + unit tests (due +24h)
- hao: add a lightweight kernel-selection counter to trace headers for better correlation (due +48h)
- mira: add alert for kernel_selection_time > 20% of CPU wall in 5m windows (monitoring)
- sylvia: collaborate with SRE to add per-node kv_cache eviction telemetry to detect noisy neighbors (due +72h)
raj: created issue RW-10234 and PR draft, tagging reviewers
eli: nice triage — will follow up in next runtime sync. Marking this thread as incident postmortem starter :memo:
opsbot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-03-08-17 (linked to RW-10234)
mira: any blips after full prod rollback? quick check: looks stable for 25m
hao: I'll keep synthetic load running for 2h to watch tail latency and kv hit ratios
sylvia: leaving notes in the rollout doc about kernel selection sensitivity to microbatching — added checklist item to run microbatch sweep on every admission-control change
eli: thanks all, great fast response. :tada:
